name: FIND
description: FIND returns the position of one text string inside another. It is case-sensitive.
tldr: Finds the position of text within another text string, case-sensitive.

parameters.name: start_num
parameters.description: The character position to start searching from (default 1).

basicExample.description: Find the position of a hyphen in a product code
basicExample.explanation: The first hyphen appears at the 4th character.

advancedExamples.title: Find a specific instance
advancedExamples.description: Find the second backslash in a path
advancedExamples.explanation: The second FIND starts searching after the first backslash.

howItWorks: FIND scans within_text for find_text and returns the position of the first match. It is case-sensitive. If the text is not found, it returns #VALUE!.

howToSteps.name: Enter text to search
howToSteps.text: Type the cell or string containing the text.

howToSteps.name: Optional start position
howToSteps.text: Add a start number to skip earlier characters.

limitations: Case-sensitive. Use SEARCH for case-insensitive search.
Returns #VALUE! if the text is not found.

commonErrors.fix: Use IFERROR to handle missing text, or use SEARCH for case-insensitive matching.

commonErrors.cause: Case mismatch because FIND is case-sensitive.
commonErrors.fix: Use SEARCH if case does not matter.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: FIND works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between FIND and SEARCH?
faq.answer: FIND is case-sensitive and does not support wildcards. SEARCH is case-insensitive and supports wildcards.

faq.question: Can FIND use wildcards?
faq.answer: No. Use SEARCH for wildcard support.
